verdict.title: Closings, deliberations, verdict (July 2, 2025) and sentencing (October 3, 2025)
verdict.case: United States v. Sean Combs, No. 24-cr-542 (S.D.N.Y.), Judge Arun Subramanian
verdict.content_note: Facts are as reported by the cited outlets. Descriptions are factual and non-graphic. The jury acquitted on the racketeering and both sex-trafficking counts; those are acquittals, not findings of the allegations.
verdict.summary: After the evidence closed on June 24, the court held a charge conference (June 25), then closing arguments (June 26-27). The jury was charged and began deliberating June 30 and returned verdicts on July 2 after about 13 hours over three days: not guilty on racketeering conspiracy and on both sex-trafficking counts; guilty on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. Bail was denied. On October 3, 2025, Combs was sentenced to 50 months, a $500,000 fine and five years of supervised release.

phases.label: Charge conference
facts: Lawyers and judge worked on jury instructions without the jury (scheduled per NBC and GMA on June 24; reporting that it took place that day rests on those schedule notes, no post-event article opened).

phases.label: Closing arguments, day 1: prosecution
facts: AUSA Christy Slavik gave the government's closing, described by GMA as nearly five hours; she argued the evidence showed a decades-long criminal enterprise and that Combs used sexually explicit videos to pressure Ventura (NPR/AP wording via Michigan Public).

phases.label: Closing arguments, day 2: defense and rebuttal
facts: Marc Agnifilo's defense closing ran about four hours (NPR: more than four hours; GMA: roughly four; AP: four hours). He called the Combs-Ventura relationship a 'great modern love story,' argued the relationships were consensual, that the case was about money, and that the male escorts were paid for their time; he disputed the arson, kidnapping and racketeering claims.
Judge Subramanian sustained an objection to the suggestion that the government was 'targeting' Combs and told jurors charging decisions are 'none of your concern' (NPR).
AUSA Maurene Comey's rebuttal said domestic violence is not a defense to sex trafficking and that the conduct ended 'in this courtroom' (GMA, NPR, AP).

phases.label: Jury charged; deliberations begin
facts: The judge instructed the jury Monday morning and deliberations began immediately after (NPR).

Jurors deliberated over five hours on June 30 (PBS NewsHour). About an hour in, the foreperson sent a note saying one juror could not follow the instructions; the judge declined to interview the juror and sent a note reminding jurors of their duty (PBS).

phases.label: Deliberations day 2
facts: About 75 minutes into the day, jurors asked to review testimony of Cassie Ventura on the 2016 Los Angeles hotel incident, a 2013 yacht incident and a New York hotel incident, plus Daniel Phillip's testimony (PBS).
Jurors asked what counts as drug distribution under the racketeering conspiracy charge; the judge planned only to remind them of earlier instructions (PBS).

Late in the day jurors reported agreement on four counts and said they were stuck on the racketeering count; the judge told them to keep deliberating (CBS, AP via KCTV5). Reports that prosecutors asked for a modified Allen charge and the defense opposed come from an earlier research pass (NPR/ABC) and were not re-opened.

phases.label: Verdict
facts: Count 1 racketeering conspiracy: not guilty. Count 2 sex trafficking (Ventura): not guilty. Count 3 transportation to engage in prostitution (Ventura): guilty. Count 4 sex trafficking (Jane): not guilty. Count 5 transportation to engage in prostitution (Jane): guilty. (CBS count-by-count; ABC7 and Fox 5 agree on the outcomes; KPBS/NPR and AP via KCTV5 confirm.)
Jury: 12 members, 8 men and 4 women (Fox 5, AP via KCTV5, KPBS/NPR). Deliberation: about 13 hours over three days (AP via KCTV5; KPBS/NPR 'more than 13 hours').

Bail: the judge denied bail; the defense had proposed a $1 million bond (CBS). He said Combs had not shown by clear and convincing evidence a lack of danger to any person or the community (AP via KCTV5). Combs remained in custody (Brooklyn Metropolitan Detention Center).

Penalties: each transportation count carries up to 10 years, up to 20 years if consecutive (Fox 5, NPR). The sex-trafficking counts carried a 15-year mandatory minimum and the racketeering count up to life (KPBS/NPR, AP).

Prosecutors' preliminary guideline estimate for the two convictions: 51 to 63 months (CBS); the defense estimated about two years (AP via KCTV5). The judge proposed October 3 for sentencing (CBS) and confirmed it in a July 9 letter (NPR).

SDNY issued a statement on the verdict (Press Release 25-155, dated July 1, updated July 2) from U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton and HSI Special Agent in Charge Ricky J. Patel; the page does not itself recite the verdict counts and speaks generally about victim-centered prosecution (DOJ).

phases.label: Post-trial motions denied
facts: Judge Subramanian denied the Rule 29 acquittal motion and a new-trial motion (TheWrap, reporting the written opinion). The court's own opinion PDF was located in search (transcripts.nysd.uscourts.gov) but was not opened in this pass.

phases.label: Sentencing
facts: Sentence: 50 months (4 years, 2 months) in federal prison; $500,000 fine (the maximum for these counts); 5 years of supervised release (NPR, GMA, AP via KSAT, NBC New York; supervised release per NPR, AP, NBC New York).

Requests: prosecution at least 11 years 3 months (135 months) (NPR, AP); defense no more than 14 months / immediate release (NPR, AP, GMA). Probation's guideline range: about 5 years 10 months to 7 years 3 months (AP via KSAT).

Judge's reasoning: a substantial sentence was needed to 'send a message to abusers and victims alike that exploitation and violence against women is met with real accountability' (NPR); 'a history of good works cannot wash away the record in this case' (GMA); Combs 'paid for and organized these acts' and the conduct went on over a decade 'with tremendous frequency' (AP, GMA). He kept a coercion enhancement citing threats to release recordings (AP via KSAT).
Credit: for time held since the September 2024 arrest (about a year) (NPR, GMA, NBC New York). Estimated time remaining: about 2.5 years (NPR) or roughly 3 years (AP) - estimates differ.

Combs apologized to Cassie Ventura, Jane and domestic-violence survivors; six of his seven children addressed the court; the witness 'Mia' withdrew from speaking after a defense objection (AP, NPR). Defense said it would appeal (NBC New York; AP: 14 days to file notice).
A DOJ/SDNY press release for the sentencing was searched for and not found in this pass.
